flashcards.q: What is the Abstract Factory pattern?
flashcards.a: A creational pattern that creates FAMILIES of related/dependent objects without specifying concrete classes.

flashcards.q: What is Abstract Factory also known as?
What are the 5 participants in Abstract Factory?
flashcards.a: 1) AbstractFactory, 2) ConcreteFactory, 3) AbstractProduct, 4) ConcreteProduct, 5) Client (uses only abstractions).

flashcards.q: How does Abstract Factory differ from Factory Method?
flashcards.a: Abstract Factory: creates FAMILIES of products using composition, multiple methods. Factory Method: creates ONE product type using inheritance, single method.

flashcards.q: When should you use Abstract Factory?
flashcards.a: When you need families of related products that must work together (e.g., UI themes, cross-platform components, database providers).

flashcards.q: When should you NOT use Abstract Factory?
flashcards.a: When you only need one product type (use Factory Method), products aren't related, or for simple object creation.

flashcards.q: What is the key principle of Abstract Factory?
flashcards.a: 'Create families of related objects together' - The factory creates multiple products that work together.

flashcards.q: Name 3 real-world examples of Abstract Factory.
flashcards.a: 1) Cross-platform UI frameworks (React Native, Flutter), 2) ORM database providers (Sequelize, TypeORM), 3) Theme systems (Material-UI dark/light).

flashcards.q: What is a common pitfall with Abstract Factory?
flashcards.a: Mixing products from different families - always use products from the SAME factory instance.

flashcards.q: What is the main disadvantage of Abstract Factory?
flashcards.a: Adding new product types requires modifying the abstract factory interface and ALL concrete factories.

flashcards.q: How can Abstract Factory be combined with Singleton?
flashcards.a: Factory itself can be a Singleton, or factories can create Singleton products.

flashcards.q: What SOLID principle does Abstract Factory support?
flashcards.a: Open/Closed Principle - easy to add new product families without modifying existing code (but not new product types).
